Hugo Simberg was born in Hamina, Finland, and studied art in Helsinki and Paris. He lived mainly in Finland and painted strange, gentle scenes full of angels, devils, and skeletons, often with a wink of humor. His work blends Finnish folk tales with Symbolism. He died in 1917 at age 43.

Arthur Hughes was born in London and was an English painter linked to the Pre-Raphaelites. He is best known for glowing, romantic scenes of young lovers and medieval stories. He worked in London and in the countryside, and he also illustrated children's books. He died in 1915.

Franz Xaver Winterhalter was born in a small village in Germany's Black Forest and became one of the most famous painters of royalty in Europe. He worked for Queen Victoria, Napoleon III and many royal courts in Paris, London and Germany. His portraits show glittering silks and graceful poses. He died in Frankfurt in 1873.

Élisabeth Louise Vigée Le Brun was born in Paris, the daughter of a painter, and became a famous portraitist at only 20. She painted Queen Marie Antoinette and fled France during the Revolution, working in Italy, Austria, Russia and England. She was one of the most successful women artists in history. She died in Paris in 1842.

Anna Bilińska-Bohdanowicz was born in Ukraine, then part of the Russian Empire, to a Polish family and studied in Saint Petersburg, Munich and Paris. She lived in Warsaw and was one of the first Polish women to win international acclaim as a painter. She painted portraits and scenes in a modern style. She died young, in 1893, at age 39.

Joshua Reynolds was born in Plympton, England, and became the first president of the Royal Academy of Arts in London. He was the most famous portrait painter of Britain in the 1700s, and he painted kings, writers, and children. He gave important lectures about art and was knighted. He died in London in 1792.

Edmund Blair Leighton was born in London and became famous for painting romantic scenes from the Middle Ages and the Regency period. He studied at the Royal Academy and lived in London. His paintings of knights and ladies are widely reproduced. He died in 1922.

Edwin Landseer was born in London and showed an extraordinary talent for drawing animals as a child. He became Queen Victoria's favorite animal painter, and he created the bronze lions at the base of Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square. He painted dogs, horses, and stags with great warmth. He died in London in 1873.

Anne Vallayer-Coster was born in Paris and became famous for lifelike still-life paintings of flowers, fruit and musical instruments. She was admitted to the French Royal Academy at 26 and also painted portraits. She worked for Queen Marie Antoinette. She died in Paris in 1818.

Carl Kahler was born in Linz, Austria, and emigrated to the United States, where he worked in San Francisco. He painted landscapes, horses and animals. His giant painting of 42 cats made him famous, and he took three years to complete it. He died in 1906.

George Stubbs was born in Liverpool, England, and taught himself to paint. He studied horse anatomy by dissecting horses and published a famous book about it. He became Britain's finest painter of horses and other animals. He died in London in 1806.

Francisco Pradilla y Ortiz was born in a small village in Aragón, Spain, and trained in Madrid and Rome. He became famous for large history paintings of kings and queens. He served as director of the Prado Museum. He died in Madrid in 1921.

Juan Luna was born in the Philippines and studied art in Manila, Madrid and Rome. His enormous painting 'Spoliarium' won a gold medal in Madrid in 1884, and made him a hero to Filipinos. He lived in Spain and France and supported Philippine independence. He died in Hong Kong in 1899.

Franz Marc was born in Munich, Germany, and loved painting animals as a symbol of purity. He co-founded the Blue Rider group with Wassily Kandinsky, and he used bold colors like blue and yellow to express feelings. He lived in Bavaria. He died in World War I in 1916 at age 36.

Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was born in Venice and became the greatest Italian painter of the 1700s. He painted huge, airy ceilings full of angels, gods and clouds in churches and palaces in Italy, Germany and Spain. His light, bright colors defined the last great age of Venetian painting. He died in Madrid in 1770.

Władysław Podkowiński was born in Warsaw, Poland, and was a leading Impressionist and Symbolist painter. He studied in Warsaw and Paris, and he is remembered for the shocking 'Frenzy of Exultations.' He died young, at 29, in 1895.

Roberto Ferruzzi was born in what is now Croatia and lived in Italy, mostly in Venice and nearby. He painted people and village scenes. His painting 'Madonnina' made him a celebrity when it won a prize in 1897. He died in 1934.

John Martin was born in Northumberland, England, and made huge, dramatic paintings of disasters from the Bible and history. His work was hugely popular in London in the 1820s and 1830s, as thrilling as a movie. He also designed engineering schemes for his city. He died on the Isle of Man in 1854.

Sofie Ribbing was born in Sweden and became a painter and teacher who lived in Sweden, Denmark, and Norway. She studied in Copenhagen and was known for scenes of children and family life. She was one of the notable Scandinavian women painters of her era. She died in 1894.

Camille Pissarro was born on the island of St. Thomas in the Caribbean and moved to France as a teen. He was the oldest of the Impressionists and a father figure and teacher to many younger painters, including Cézanne. He painted farms, villages and city streets in France. He died in Paris in 1903.

Adolph von Menzel was born in Breslau (now Wrocław, Poland) and lived most of his life in Berlin. He was Germany's greatest realist painter and an amazing draftsman. He painted history scenes, factories and daily life. He was a very short man who worked until his death in 1905.

Louis-Michel van Loo was born in Toulon, France, to a family of painters. He worked in Paris and also in Spain as the court painter to King Philip V. His portraits show silk, lace and royal splendor. He died in Paris in 1771.

William Hogarth was born in London and became one of Britain's best-known painters and engravers. He made funny, sharp pictures about the follies of society, often in sets of prints that tell a story. He also championed the rights of artists. He died in London in 1764.

James Ensor was born in Ostend, Belgium, and lived there nearly his whole life. He painted bizarre carnival masks, skeletons, and crowds in bright, shocking colors. His strange work was ahead of its time, and he became a hero for modern artists. He died in Ostend in 1949.

Vasily Pukirev was born in the Tula region of Russia and became a painter and teacher in Moscow. His most famous painting, 'The Unequal Marriage,' criticized forced marriages. It was a sensation, and he later taught at the Moscow School of Painting. He died in 1890.

Henry Holiday was born in London and was a painter, designer and stained-glass artist. He was influenced by the Pre-Raphaelites. He also illustrated Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Hunting of the Snark'. He died in London in 1927.

Berthe Morisot was born in Bourges, France, and studied painting with Corot. She exhibited in the first Impressionist show in 1874 and was one of the movement's leading figures. She married Eugène Manet, the brother of Édouard Manet, and lived in Paris. She painted women, children and gardens with a light, fresh touch.

Isaac Levitan was born in Lithuania to a Jewish family and grew up in Moscow, where he studied painting. He became one of Russia's greatest landscape painters, known for his poetic scenes of rivers, forests and quiet villages. He often painted along the Volga River. He died in Moscow in 1900, at age 39.

Henri Fantin-Latour was born in Grenoble, France, and spent most of his life in Paris. He was a friend of Manet and the Impressionists, though his own style was more traditional. He painted lovely flowers and group portraits of artists and musicians. He died in 1904.

Olga Boznańska was born in Kraków, Poland, and studied in Munich and Paris, where she lived for much of her life. She became one of the most important Polish painters, with a soft, gray-toned style, and she painted many portraits. She was widely admired in Paris. She died there in 1940.

Martinus Rørbye was born in Drammen, Norway, and moved to Denmark as a child. He was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age and traveled to Italy, Greece, and Turkey. He painted precise scenes of streets, interiors and windows. He died in Copenhagen in 1848.

Laurits Andersen Ring was born in a village in Denmark and became a leading Danish painter. He is known for quiet, thoughtful scenes of country life and portraits of his family. He lived and worked in the Danish countryside. He died in 1933.

Johan Christian Dahl was born in Bergen, Norway, and became known as the father of Norwegian landscape painting. He lived most of his life in Dresden, Germany, where he was a friend of Caspar David Friedrich. He painted clouds, mountains and fjords with great realism. He died in Dresden in 1857.

Harald Slott-Møller was born in Denmark, near Copenhagen, and was a painter and designer. He is known for dreamy Symbolist pictures and portraits. He lived in Copenhagen and was married to the painter Agnes Slott-Møller. He died in 1937.

Philipp Veit was born in Berlin and became a painter in the Nazarene movement, a group who admired the art of medieval and Renaissance Germany and Italy. He lived in Rome, Frankfurt and Mainz. He was also a museum director. He died in Mainz in 1877.

Gilbert Stuart was born in Rhode Island and became America's best-known portrait painter. He painted George Washington and other leaders of the young United States. He lived for years in London and Dublin before returning to the U.S. He died in Boston in 1828.

Jacques Amans was born in Maastricht, in the Netherlands, and worked as a portrait painter in France and the United States. He lived in New Orleans for several years in the 1830s and painted many local families. He returned to Paris, where he died in 1888.

Jean-Baptiste Camille Corot was born in Paris and spent much of his life painting the French countryside and trips to Italy. His silvery, misty landscapes influenced Impressionist painters such as Monet and Pissarro. He was known as a kind and generous man. He died in Paris in 1875.

Johann Heinrich Wilhelm Tischbein was born in Haina, Germany, to a family of painters. He lived in Rome and Naples and became a friend of the poet Goethe. He painted portraits and scenes from mythology. He died in Eutin, Germany, in 1829.

Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin was born in Paris, the son of a cabinet-maker. He became one of the greatest painters of still lifes and quiet scenes of everyday life in 1700s France. He worked slowly and carefully with a soft touch. He spent his entire life in Paris.

George Peter Alexander Healy was born in Boston and became a portrait painter who worked in Paris, Rome, Chicago and Washington. He painted American presidents and the kings and queens of Europe. He lived long in Europe before settling in Chicago. He died there in 1894.

Christoffer Wilhelm Eckersberg was born in southern Denmark and became the 'father of Danish painting.' He studied in Paris and Rome and taught many painters in Copenhagen. He painted portraits, ships, and clear, bright scenes of Rome. He died in Copenhagen in 1853.

Edward Savage was born in Massachusetts and was an American painter and engraver. He painted George Washington from life and made popular prints of his work. He lived in Philadelphia, New York and Boston. He died in 1817.

Nikolai Ge was born in Voronezh, Russia, and studied in Saint Petersburg and Italy. He painted powerful scenes from history and religion with dramatic light and strong emotion. Later in life he lived on a farm in Ukraine. He died in 1894.

Mikhail Nesterov was born in Ufa, Russia, and became a leading painter of religious and spiritual scenes. He painted frescoes in churches and created poetic pictures of saints in Russian landscapes. He lived through the Russian Revolution and continued painting in Moscow. He died there in 1942.

Abanindranath Tagore was born in Kolkata (Calcutta), India, into a famous family that included the poet Rabindranath Tagore. He founded the Bengal School of art, which revived Indian painting styles. His work inspired the movement for India's independence. He died in Kolkata in 1951.

Anna Ancher was born in Skagen, Denmark, the daughter of an innkeeper. She became one of the greatest painters of the Skagen artists' colony, known for her use of light, and for her portraits and interiors. She married the painter Michael Ancher and lived her whole life in Skagen. She died there in 1935.

August Malmström was born in Sweden and became a painter of Nordic legends, fairy tales and landscapes. He studied in Stockholm and Düsseldorf. He later directed the Swedish National Museum's art school. He died in Stockholm in 1901.

August Strindberg was born in Stockholm, Sweden, and is best known as one of the world's greatest playwrights and novelists. He also painted dramatic, stormy landscapes in his later years, which were far ahead of their time. He lived in Sweden, Germany, France and Denmark. He died in Stockholm in 1912.

Kolë Idromeno was born in Shkodër, Albania, and became a painter, architect and sculptor. He studied in Italy and is regarded as a pioneer of modern Albanian art. He designed buildings in his hometown. He died in Shkodër in 1939.

Jean-Baptiste Greuze was born in Tournus, France, and moved to Paris, where he became famous for sentimental paintings of family life and young girls with moral messages. He was admired by the philosopher Diderot. His popularity faded after the French Revolution. He died in Paris in 1805.

Suzanne Valadon was born in a small town in France and moved to Paris as a girl. She worked as a circus performer and an artist's model for Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec before teaching herself to paint. She became the first woman admitted to the French National Society of Fine Arts. She lived in Montmartre and died in Paris in 1938.

Alfred Sisley was born in Paris to English parents and was one of the key Impressionist painters. He painted quiet landscapes along the Seine River and in small villages near Paris. He lived most of his life in France but remained a British citizen. He died in Moret-sur-Loing in 1899.

Honoré Daumier was born in Marseille, France, and grew up in Paris. He was famous for his satirical cartoons that poked fun at politicians, and he created thousands of prints. He also painted sympathetic pictures of working people. He lost his sight late in life and died in 1879.

Richard Dadd was born in Chatham, England, and became a talented painter before he fell seriously ill in his twenties. He spent the rest of his life in hospitals, where he kept painting amazing, tiny, detailed fairy pictures. He lived in Bethlem and then Broadmoor Hospital. He died in 1886.

Akseli Gallen-Kallela was born in Pori, Finland, and became the country's most famous painter. He painted scenes from the Kalevala, Finland's national epic, and studied in Paris. He lived in Finland and traveled to Africa and the United States. He died in Stockholm in 1931.

Vincenzo Camuccini was born in Rome and became one of Italy's leading Neoclassical painters. He painted big history scenes and was in charge of the Vatican's paintings. He was also a collector. He died in Rome in 1844.

Johann Friedrich Overbeck was born in Lübeck, Germany, and moved to Rome, where he led the Nazarenes, a group of artists inspired by medieval and early Renaissance painting. He lived in a former monastery with his friends. He stayed in Rome the rest of his life and died there in 1869.

Constantin Hansen was born in Rome to Danish parents and grew up in Copenhagen. He was a leading painter of the Danish Golden Age and painted portraits, historical scenes and murals. He also visited Italy. He died near Copenhagen in 1880.

Albert Bierstadt was born in Germany and raised in Massachusetts. He traveled west with survey expeditions and painted vast landscapes of the Rocky Mountains and Yosemite. His work was admired by huge crowds in the East. He lived in New York and died there in 1902.

James Tissot was born in Nantes, France, and moved to London, where he painted fashionable scenes of Victorian life. Later he traveled to the Holy Land and made a famous series of illustrations of the Bible. He was a very successful artist. He died in France in 1902.

Evelyn De Morgan was born in London and studied at the Slade School of Art. She was a Pre-Raphaelite painter who painted glowing allegories about peace, war and the spirit. She lived in London and Florence and was also a pacifist and a supporter of women's rights. She died in 1919.

Kuzma Petrov-Vodkin was born in a small town on the Volga River in Russia, and trained in Moscow, Saint Petersburg, and Paris. He used Russian icon painting as inspiration for his bold, simple style. He later taught in Saint Petersburg (then Leningrad). He died there in 1939.

Vasily Polenov was born in Saint Petersburg, Russia, and became a leading landscape painter and teacher. He traveled in Europe and the Middle East. He built an estate on the Oka River that is now a museum. He died in 1927.

Edvard Isto was born in northern Finland and became a painter who studied in Helsinki and Paris. He is best known for 'The Attack,' which became a symbol of Finnish resistance. He died in Helsinki in 1905, at the age of 40.

Charles Demuth was born in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, and studied art in Philadelphia and Paris. He was a leading American modernist known for crisp, precise paintings of buildings and factories. He lived with diabetes for most of his adult life. He died in Lancaster in 1935.

Marie Spartali Stillman was born in London to a Greek family and became one of the few women to be a respected Pre-Raphaelite painter. She studied with Ford Madox Brown. She modeled for other artists, too. She lived in London and Italy and died in 1927.

Mariano Fortuny Marsal was born in Reus, Spain, and became one of the best-known Spanish painters of the 1800s. He traveled to Morocco and painted bright, detailed scenes. He lived in Rome and Madrid, and died young in Rome in 1874, at age 36.

Albert Edelfelt was born in Finland to a Swedish family and studied in Antwerp and Paris. He painted portraits, scenes of Finnish life, and historical subjects. He was one of the most famous Finnish painters. He died in Finland in 1905.

Frederick Sandys was born in Norwich, England, and became a painter and illustrator associated with the Pre-Raphaelites. He was famous for detailed portraits of beautiful women. He lived in London, and he died there in 1904.

Jacek Malczewski was born in Radom, Poland, and became a leading Symbolist painter. He studied in Kraków and Paris and often painted himself in dreamlike scenes full of Polish folklore and history. He lived in Kraków, where he later taught. He died there in 1929.

Anne-Louis Girodet was born in Montargis, France, and studied under Jacques-Louis David. He became a leader of French Romanticism with dreamy, mysterious paintings. He lived in Rome and Paris. He died in Paris in 1824.

Nicolaas Pieneman was born in Amersfoort, in the Netherlands, and became a portrait and history painter in Amsterdam. He painted royalty, battle scenes and a famous picture of the arrest of the Javanese prince Diponegoro. He died in Amsterdam in 1860.

William Orpen was born near Dublin, Ireland, and became a leading portrait painter in London. He served as an official war artist in World War I and painted the Paris Peace Conference. He died in London in 1931.

Edouard Louis Dubufe was born in Paris to a family of painters. He painted portraits and historical scenes for the French court and nobility. He was a successful society painter in the era of Napoleon III. He died in 1883.

Giovanni Antonio Canal, known as Canaletto, was born in Venice and painted its canals, palaces, and festivals with great precision. His views were popular with wealthy British visitors on their tours of Italy, and he lived in London for several years. His paintings are still the way many people picture Venice. He died in Venice in 1768.

Pierre Auguste Cot was born in the south of France and became a popular painter in Paris. He studied with Bouguereau and painted romantic and mythological subjects. His paintings were very popular in America. He died in 1883.

Wilhelm Bendz was born in Odense, Denmark, and studied in Copenhagen. He painted lively portraits of his artist friends and finely detailed scenes of daily life. He died of an illness at only 28 in Vicenza, Italy, in 1832.

Peder Balke was born on an island in Norway and became a painter who started out as a house painter. He traveled to Norway's far north and painted bold, simple pictures of the sea and mountains. His work went unnoticed in his lifetime but is admired today. He died in Christiania (Oslo) in 1887.

John Steuart Curry was born on a farm in Kansas and became one of the main painters of the Regionalist movement, which celebrated the American Midwest. He painted farm life, storms and big moments from history. He also painted murals for the Kansas State Capitol. He died in Wisconsin in 1946.

Ernst Ludwig Kirchner was born in Aschaffenburg, Germany, and trained as an architect before he became a founder of the group Die Brücke ('The Bridge'). He lived in Dresden and Berlin and later in the Swiss Alps near Davos. His jagged, colorful paintings made him a star of German Expressionism. He died in Switzerland in 1938.

Alphonse Mucha was born in Ivančice, in what is now the Czech Republic. He moved to Paris and became world-famous for his elegant Art Nouveau posters. Later in his life he returned to Prague and painted a huge series of paintings called the Slav Epic. He died in 1939.

Walenty Wańkowicz was born in a village in what is now Belarus and studied in Vilnius. He became a Polish painter famous for portraits of poets, including Adam Mickiewicz. He lived in Saint Petersburg and in Paris. He died in Paris in 1842.

Marie-Guillemine Benoist was born in Paris and studied with Vigée Le Brun and Jacques-Louis David. She was one of the leading women painters of her time and exhibited at the Paris Salon. Her 'Portrait of Madeleine' is one of the most celebrated works of the French Revolution era. She died in Paris in 1826.

Angelica Kauffman was born in Chur, Switzerland, and was a child prodigy who traveled across Europe as a teen artist. She lived in Italy and London, where she became a founding member of the Royal Academy of Arts. She painted portraits and scenes from myth and history. She died in Rome in 1807.

Odilon Redon was born in Bordeaux, France, and spent most of his life in Paris. He began with strange, dreamlike black-and-white drawings, then later painted flowers and myths in luminous color. His art was admired by Symbolists and later by the Surrealists. He died in Paris in 1916.

Ivan Grohar was born in what is now Slovenia and became one of the country's best-known painters. He painted farmers and landscapes in bright, bold colors. He studied in Ljubljana and Munich. He died in Ljubljana in 1911.
